Body:
By submitting this issue you are acknowledging that any information regarding this issue will be publicly available.

If you have privacy concerns, please email [conformance-tools@fidoalliance.org](mailto:conformance-tools@fidoalliance.org)

## FIRST PRE CHECK

- [ ] I SOLEMNLY SWEAR THAT I HAVE SEARCHED [DOCUMENTATION](https://github.com/fido-alliance/conformance-test-tools-resources/tree/master/docs) AND WAS NOT ABLE TO RESOLVE MY ISSUE

- [ ] U2F 1.1

NOTE: UAF 1.0 certification have been officially sunset. U2F 1.2 only supported version of U2F.

## What is your implementation class?

- [ ] Security Key / FIDO2 / U2F authenticators
- [ X ] Server

- [ ] UAF Client

If you are platform authenticator vendor, please email [conformance-tools@fidoalliance.org](mailto:conformance-tools@fidoalliance.org)

## What is the version of the tool are you using?
FIDO Conformance Tools v1.7.17

## What is the OS and the version are you running?
macOS Sonoma 14.2

For desktop tools
- [ X ] OSX
- [ ] Windows
- [ ] Linux

For UAF mobile tools
- [ ] iOS
- [ ] Android

## Issue description
The final test case for Metadata Service Tests succeeds when it is supposed to fail. I don't believe the CRL is populated (at all).

The test case is:
F-5 Send a valid ServerAuthenticatorAttestationResponse with FULL "packed" attestation for metadata from MDS3 who's metadata service leaf certificate is revoked, and check that serve returns an error

I captured an attestation result body, which showed a registration for AAGUID: BD794810-6113-4F57-A6B4-ECE5D1244AB2
I found the corresponding MDS3 server entry that contains this AAGUID (attached as e3145fb35e4349e9f0718b60a224616019a456c7722a0926520847b0c98d6672.jwt.txt).
I looked into the JWT header, extracted x5c, and then produced PEM files for each of the two entries (x5c0.pem.txt and x5c1.pem.txt attached).
x5c0.pem is the leaf certificate, and is signed by x5c1.pem which is the intermediate. The intermediate is signed by MDSROOT.crt. 

The test case says the leaf certificate (i.e. x5c0.pem) is revoked. Looking at this cert in more detail we see:
 - The certificate serial number is: 04:80:67:49:de:30:7b:bd:51:75:a2:6d:73:f5:f3
 - The certificate extensions identify the following CRL distribution point: https://mds3.certinfra.fidoalliance.org/crl/MDSCA-1.crl
 - Trying to retrieve that URL returns an empty response (i.e. no CRL at the provided distribution point)

If this leaf certificate is indeed revoked, then I believe a valid CRL containing its serial number should be retrievable from the CRL distribution point identified in the certificate.

Title: Groth16 verifier Solidity generator method
Body:
Compatible with the proofs generated by https://github.com/arkworks-rs/groth16 .

This is for the onchain (Ethereum's EVM) decider case.

The idea is to end up having a library method that given a Groth16's trustedsetup, it outputs the solidity code that verifies the commitments. Similar to what [snarkjs does](https://github.com/iden3/snarkjs#25-turn-the-verifier-into-a-smart-contract), but without being a cli.

An implementation of a Groth16 Solidity verifier (non arkworks compatible) can be found at https://github.com/iden3/snarkjs/blob/master/templates/verifier_groth16.sol.ejs

Note that this is not yet the CLI, this is a library method. The CLI will be done once the KZG & Groth16 verifier generators are ready, the issue to track the CLI task is https://github.com/privacy-scaling-explorations/folding-schemes/issues/57

Title: Accessibility hints
Body:
Fortunately there is a lot we can already do to improve the accessibility of websites. Client hints may even provide another way to inform us of what a user needs. I do believe there is a risk to privacy (though it would be opt-in), but I believe the gains may be worth it. Hopefully this is the right place - and I didn't read over anything related - for such a discussion.

I'm thinking about headers such as `Sec-CH-UA-Perceivable`, `Sec-CH-UA-Operable`, etc. as per  [WACG](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/quickref/)

A few examples:

A webpage may use such information to pre-apply certain [changeable] preferences for users, such as font-size, contrast, item spacing. It could also provide a simpler layout, i.e. for screen readers and such. Certain JavaScript events such as mouseover could be adjusted to click, i.e. for certain motor disabilities this _may_ be useful, etcetera.

FWIW, I'm not advocating that developers bypass the WACG or other standards.

Advisory [CVE-2025-27090](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-27090) references a vulnerability in the following Go modules:

| Module |
| - |
| [github.com/BishopFox/sliver](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/BishopFox/sliver) |

Description:
Sliver is an open source cross-platform adversary emulation/red team framework, it can be used by organizations of all sizes to perform security testing. The reverse port forwarding in sliver teamserver allows the implant to open a reverse tunnel on the sliver teamserver without verifying if the operator instructed the implant to do so. The only impact that has been shown is the exposure of the server's IP address to a third party. This issue has been addressed in version 1.5.43 and all users are advised to upgrade. There are no known workarounds for this vulnerability.

References:
- ADVISORY: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-27090
- FIX: https://github.com/BishopFox/sliver/commit/0f340a25cf3d496ed870dae7da39eab4427bc16f

No existing reports found with this module or alias.

Title: Mitigate Rust view server crashes when using load-balanced GRPC endpoints
Body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Sometimes the Rust view server will crash when doing operations with an error like


> `Error: status: Internal, message: "Worker failed: status: Unavailable, message: \"error querying abci: response error\\n\\nCaused by:\\n    Internal error: height 267621 must be less than or equal to the current blockchain height 267620 (code: -32603)\\n\\nLocation:\\n    /usr/local/cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-6f17d22bba15001f/flex-error-0.4.4/src/tracer_impl/eyre.rs:10:9\", details: [], metadata: MetadataMap { headers: {\"access-control-allow-credentials\": \"true\", \"access-control-allow-headers\": \"*\", \"access-control-allow-methods\": \"*\", \"access-control-allow-origin\": \"*\", \"access-control-expose-headers\": \"grpc-status,grpc-message,grpc-status-details-bin\", \"content-type\": \"application/grpc\", \"date\": \"Thu, 16 Nov 2023 22:29:43 GMT\", \"vary\": \"origin\", \"vary\": \"access-control-request-method\", \"vary\": \"access-control-request-headers\", \"content-length\": \"0\"} }", details: [], metadata: MetadataMap { headers: {"content-type": "application/grpc"} }`

The cause of this is that the view server is making requests to a load-balanced RPC. It gets notified of data in a new block. Then it makes follow-up requests about that data. But those requests are routed to a different backend which hasn't learned about the data yet, erroring out.

Ideally, the view server would be robust against this, so we don't accidentally place demands for strong consensus on RPC clusters.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Investigate places where this happens and attempt to mitigate. This might be better to do after restructuring the view server code to have 2-phase sync.

Title: Add automated Cypress tests for Privacy Center configuration
Body:
### Is your feature request related to a specific problem?

We support a ton of customization options for the Privacy Center to swap out text, add new paragraphs, hide/show actions, etc. However, our Cypress suite currently doesn't exercise most of these options, so there's a regression risk here as we continue to add new features to the app!

### Describe the solution you'd like

Update /fides/clients/privacy-center/cypress/e2e/home.cy.ts with tests to cover all the various configuration options, and ensure that the expected text/logos/buttons/etc. are well covered by tests.

The refactor in https://github.com/ethyca/fides/pull/3105 makes this much more manageable, since the configuration is now loaded at runtime so we can easily mutate the Redux store and test all kinds of different variations!

Title: Presentation and Organization of the Standard
Body:
I recommend making a few minor changes to improve the organization and presentation of the Standard. 

- I think adding numbers to the test names, criteria and indicators will make it easier for researchers and stakeholders to make references to the Standard. 

- It would be great to have one test name correspond to one criterion. Currently, that is the case for all the test names but “Governance” and “Data Retention and Deletion”. The “Governance” test has 6 criteria, each includes several corresponding indicators. Consider breaking “Governance” down into 6 test names to correspond with each of the 6 criteria. For example, we could add a test name “Governance Oversight” for the following criterion: “The company or organization's senior leadership exercises oversight over how its policies and practices affect freedom of expression and privacy.”  This approach (one test name=one criterion) will simplify the format of the Standard and our effort to have a consistent numbering system for the Standard. 

- We need alignment between criteria and their indicators to avoid confusion. For example, there is no clear alignment between the “Governance” criteria and their indicators. Unless researchers are familiar with RDR’s G indicators, they will have a hard time figuring out which indicator corresponds to which criterion, especially without numbering. 

- We need to use a consistent style throughout the Standard. Currently, some indicators and procedure overview are presented in full sentences, while others are not. Similarly, some of the criteria are written with the user as the subject, while others are written with the company or the product as the subject. 

- I also understand that there many different ways to organize the Standard. However, I want to highlight two test names that stand out as outliers in the Ownership category—Process for Terms of Service Enforcement and Transparency about Terms of Service Enforcement. These two seem to fit better in the Governance and Compliance category.

Title: [MASWE-0018] Cryptographic Keys Access Not Restricted
Body:
## Description

Create a new risk for "Cryptographic Keys Access Not Restricted (MASVS-CRYPTO-2)" using the following information:

Ensuring that cryptographic keys are accessible only under strict conditions, such as when the device is unlocked by an authenticated user, within secure application contexts, or for limited periods of time, is critical to maintaining the confidentiality and integrity of encrypted data.



Create "`risks/MASVS-CRYPTO/2-***-****/crypto-key-access-not-restricted/risk.md`" including the following content:

```yaml
---
title: Cryptographic Keys Access Not Restricted
alias: crypto-key-access-not-restricted
platform: [android, ios]
profiles: [L2]
mappings:
  masvs-v2: [MASVS-CRYPTO-2, MASVS-AUTH-2, MASVS-AUTH-3]
  mastg-v1: []

---

## Overview

## Impact

## Modes of Introduction

## Mitigations

```

**To complete the sections follow the guidelines from [Writing MASTG Risks & Tests](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EMsVdfrDBAu0gmjWAUEs60q-fWaOmDB5oecY9d9pOlg/edit?usp=sharing)**

Use at least the following references:

- <https://developer.android.com/reference/android/security/keystore/KeyGenParameterSpec.Builder#setUnlockedDeviceRequired(boolean)>
- <https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/ksecattraccessiblewhenunlockedthisdeviceonly>
- <https://developer.android.com/training/sign-in/biometric-auth#prompt-the-user-to-authenticate-with-biometrics>
- <https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/keychain_services/keychain_items/restricting_keychain_item_accessibility#2974973>

When creating the corresponding tests, use the following areas to guide you:

- from a Background Process
- locked device (iOS kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly, Android setUnlockedDeviceRequired)
- time-based access (duration)
- Require User Presence
- application-specific password
- biometric authentication
- key use restricted e.g. requiring user auth with biometrics, User Presence.
- especially for sensitive operations
- keys restricted/authorized for a duration of time or specific crypto operation, etc.

**MASTG v1 Refactoring:**

If the risk has a MASVS v1 ID, you can use it to [search for related tests in the MASTG](https://mas.owasp.org/MASTG/tests/) and use them as input to define your risks and associated tests.



## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The risk has been created in the correct directory (`risks/MASVS-CRYPTO/2-***-****/crypto-key-access-not-restricted/risk.md`)
- [ ] The risk content follows the [guidelines](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EMsVdfrDBAu0gmjWAUEs60q-fWaOmDB5oecY9d9pOlg/edit?usp=sharing)
- [ ] At least one GitHub Issue has been created for the corresponding tests (derived from "Modes of Introduction")
- [ ] The risk indicates the related MASTG v1 tests in its metadata.

Title: VulnerabilityManifest in workload namespace
Body:
## Overview
Currenty Kubescape operator saves VulnerabilityManifest in the kubescape namespace. The VulnerabilityManifestSummary is saved in the workload namespace. 

## Problem
Users need to have access rights to the kubescape namespace in order to view detailed findings. This is an issue when users have limited access rights due to cluster RBAC restrictions. In organizations where clusters are managed by platform teams, users only get access to their own namespaces to manage their own workloads. Currently we have to give users access rights to the Kubescape namespace and we would rather not do that. 

## Solution
Make the VulnerabilityManifest available in the workload namespace. Cluster users will not need to have access anymore to the kubescape namespace in order to view Vulnerability details. 
For compatibility we might make the VulnerabiltyManifest available in the kubescape namespace as well. 

## Related Issue 
VulnerabilityManifestSummary contains references to VulnerabilityManifest , and these references suggest to find the VulnerabilityManifest in the workload namespace (vulnerabilitiesRef.all.namespace and vulnerabilitiesRef.relevant.namespace are set to the workload namespace). This seems to be inconsistent.

Title: headsup: I intend to relax some prefs
Body:
this will get rid of ~~4~~ 3 (Ipv6 wasn't listed) of the [common items in the wiki](https://github.com/arkenfox/user.js/wiki/3.2-Overrides-[Common])

speak if you want to

---

### DRM - move to optional hardening

I have lived without DRM in my everyday main FF since we first disabled it. I do not stream any content (Netflix, Disney, Hulu etc). But I do read a lot, and some of that is news, and some of that news comes with video, and sometimes that shit won't work (not always because its DRM - I use a pretty hard uBO), and all I end up doing is flicking over to my nightly (which is default + uBO + sanitizing on close) and fucking loading it anyway. 

I get that DRM is a propriety and closed source, but honestly, for our threat model, disabling it is just a PITA and massive overkill. If this is your issue, then use Tor Browser. And I'm sure I'm the exception not the norm re streaming, so I know I've said users could just use a secondary browser, but that's not always easy for some people if they want a second gecko, dealing with profiles and installs and running concurrently.

So heads up, this WILL be moved to optional hardening. Those who do not want DRM can easily add an override

```js
/* 2022: disable all DRM content (EME: Encryption Media Extension)
 * Optionally hide the setting which also disables the DRM prompt
 * [SETUP-WEB] e.g. Netflix, Amazon Prime, Hulu, HBO, Disney+, Showtime, Starz, DirectTV
 * [SETTING] General>DRM Content>Play DRM-controlled content
 * [TEST] https://bitmovin.com/demos/drm
 * [1] https://www.eff.org/deeplinks/2017/10/drms-dead-canary-how-we-just-lost-web-what-we-learned-it-and-what-we-need-do-next ***/
user_pref("media.eme.enabled", false);
   // user_pref("browser.eme.ui.enabled", false);
```

###  referer.XOriginPolicy - ~~make inactive~~ move to optional hardening

I plan to relax this. I don't see any real benefit for value `1`, it will unbreak fuck all IMO. So I am going to make the pref inactive. Those who want to harden can do so in their overrides. At the end of the day, most navigational "tracking" is harmless (i.e the same for everyone) and effectively blocking cross site referers just breaks "everything"

I am also going to remove any reference to Smart Referer, as I consider it abandoned. Plus it's not a good idea re CSRF see #1433 and for this reason I will not be recommending ANY referer extensions

Also, mask your IP, you dirty filthy animals

```js
/* 1601: control when to send a cross-origin referer
 * 0=always (default), 1=only if base domains match, 2=only if hosts match
 * [SETUP-WEB] Breakage: older modems/routers and some sites e.g banks, vimeo, icloud, instagram
 * If "2" is too strict, then override to "0" and use Smart Referer extension (Strict mode + add exceptions) ***/
user_pref("network.http.referer.XOriginPolicy", 2);
```

### keyword - ~~make inactive~~ move to optional opsec

Considering the default FF does not show the searchbar, the urlbar IS the searchbar. So disabling keyword is more of an obstacle than a help. I also think the chances you do a typo or leak a secret are slim to none (I think I've caught myself with about 2 in 10 years), and you would still leak that typo/secret if you used the searchbar and hit enter. And the advice "Override this if you trust and use a privacy respecting search engine" is a little weird - if users are _that_ privacy conscious (e.g. I still use google in nightly because it gets me my results) then they would have already changed engines. In other words, users are going to use the search engine they want to, and we can't change that, so to dictate out advice for keyword based on their search engine is a bit on odd, kinda. Anyway, I don't see this as anything more than user hostile for our threat model - even TB doesn't bother, because usability matters.

once again, those who wish to override it, can do so

```js
/* 0801: disable location bar using search
 * Don't leak URL typos to a search engine, give an error message instead
 * Examples: "secretplace,com", "secretplace/com", "secretplace com", "secret place.com"
 * [NOTE] This does not affect explicit user action such as using search buttons in the
 * dropdown, or using keyword search shortcuts you configure in options (e.g. "d" for DuckDuckGo)
 * [SETUP-CHROME] Override this if you trust and use a privacy respecting search engine ***/
user_pref("keyword.enabled", false);
```

### IPv6: ~~make inactive~~ - move to optional hardening

This is only an issue IMO for those using a VPN. And VPN users should be using a system wide reputable VPN like e.g. Mullvad (full disclosure, Mullvad sponsors Tor Project, and I work with them both - in fact I will be at Mullvad headquarters for a week in late October). I'm not a VPN expert, so Mullvad is the only name I could think of that I know is reputable. I assume Mullvad covers IPv6 properly (IANAE on networking shit, that's the 🐟 ). I also wonder, and IANAE, is that if the VPN fell over, you would be leaking your real IP anyway, so big deal with the mac addy? rhetorical q, don't answer

I think this line sums it up "If you are not masking your IP, then this won't make much difference."

again, users can override

```js
/* 0701: disable IPv6
SNIP
 * [1] https://www.internetsociety.org/tag/ipv6-security/ (Myths 2,4,5,6) ***/
user_pref("network.dns.disableIPv6", true);
```

[Bug - Sparrow GUI] Linux: Open transaction in external browser not working if Tor Browser is default browser
Body:
Steps to reproduce:

- Test on Ubuntu (particular a Kubuntu but I don't think the flavor and version is relevant to the issue)
- Set default application to open web links to Tor Browser in Ubuntu settings
- In Sparrow Deskstop v1.7.7. go to `Preferences` and set Block Explorer to mempool.space
- In `Transactions` tab, open detail screen of a transaction
- Click on the `Open transaction in the configured block explorer` button behind the Txid

-> Tor browser tries to open but doesn't succeed

Could be a limitation of the Tor Browser (doesn't allow external links to be opened?) but could be an issue especially in reagards to #372 since over there Tor Browser is default iirc.

## My questions

 - What can I do to fix the warnings? A big part of my dependencies is simply missing from the result table.
 - Is there a way to evaluate all the `package.json` files inside `node_modules`? According to the [documentation](https://github.com/DmitriyLewen/trivy/blob/main/docs/docs/vulnerability/detection/language.md) for filesystem scanning this is intentionally disabled. Why? I am aware that there are A LOT of files but shouldn't the users decide how long they are willing to wait for the scan to conclude?
 - Same for the `devDependencies`. Is there a way to enable NPM dev dependency scanning and if not, why?

Title: VOTE: enable Tracking Protection [Edit: and SB]
Body:
see #102 for the discussion, and make comments there, so its in one place.

This issue is just so I can get a handle on what people want. I will make a decision on when I get some reasonable numbers of votes.

Vote by adding a reaction to this post

### Proposal

In this user.js, the master branch, (we will have a lite/relaxed branch in future), to enable TP (tracking protection).

Notes:
- We recommend in numerous places that we expect users to be using uBo, which has advantages (default all windows, more comprehensive options). Despite this, as a FALLBACK for users who do not read (and one of our/my aims is to make this more accessible to everyone) and for those who do not use uBo, we should be RESPONSIBLE and enable TP (we're already responsible eg warnings etc, but we should cover as many case scenarios as possible)
- TP (at defaults) is only used in PB mode, whereas uBo is used by default on all windows. We should really MAKE people use uBo - right? - which we can still do with our warnings etc, but some people never read or are afraid of uBo etc.
- TP uses ~~the same list as uBo~~ a list (note: there are two lists, simple+strict, default is simple and we would leave it at that but include the pref for info/enforcing strict)
  * UPDATE: uBo uses multiple lists in default mode and covers almost everything TP does (and more), but there are some items only TP does (rare). No-one has done a comparison.
- TP (at defaults) and uBo do not clash in any way
- There are no issues over TP re security, privacy, or hourly connections for checks, or downloads - but for uBo users, it's redundant, that's all. [Edit: there are no issues over fingerprinting thru HSTS]
- The make up of what settings we use are irrelevant - this vote is about enabling it (either defaults, or enforcing to normal windows is irrelevant at this stage)
- We could leave this for a lite/relaxed branch, which will happen

That's about it really. Either turn TP on in this branch (which is our default branch), or wait until a lite branch.

Note: this would require approx 4 prefs to be made inactive (and reset in about:config), plus one new pref (inactive), and some changes to the wiki and the user.js's readme, and the 0400 section header description. That's about it.

:+1:  =  don't disable TP (in other words end users are at default, prefs become inactive)
:-1:  =  hell no, leave TP disabled by the user.js

| [github.com/usememos/memos](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/usememos/memos) |

Description:
The Memos application, up to version v0.24.3, allows for the embedding of markdown images with arbitrary URLs. When a user views a memo containing such an image, their browser automatically fetches the image URL without explicit user consent or interaction beyond viewing the memo. This can be exploited by an attacker to disclose the viewing user's IP address, browser User-Agent string, and potentially other request-specific information to the attacker-controlled server, leading to information disclosure and user tracking.

Title: Access to rsim via `std::map::operator[]()` is not guaranteed to be thread safe
Body:
In the simulation code [line 70](https://github.com/igmmgi/DMCfun/blob/7552278280e64dd6880a6307ddb3f5e42991697d/src/runDMC.cpp#L70) the shared map `rsim`  is accessed via `std::map::operator[]`. However, the C++ standard only ensures thread-safety for read operations (i.e. `const` functions) on STL-Containers ([see Section 26.2.2 of the C++17 standard draft version](http://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg21/docs/papers/2017/n4659.pdf)). 

For associative containers (i.e. `std::map` or `std::unordered_map`), the `operator[]()` is not considered `const` and therefore not thread safe (see the [documentation](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/container/map/operator_at), which does not include a const version of this operator). 

While this may not be an issue, it may lead to data corruption and/or crashes in rare and hard to debug circumstances.

Proposed fix: Use the `std::map::at` function, which is considered `const` for the purpose of Section 26.2.2.

Title: Allow setting l0_sensitivity and linf_sensitivity parameters (SetMaxPartitionsContributed, SetMaxContributionsPerPartition)
Body:
## Feature Description
Algorithms in PyDP are currently using default values of 1 for l0 sensitivity and linf sensitivity.
The library user needs a way to set these parameters.

## Is your feature request related to a problem?
Restaurant demo cannot be ported to the current version of PyDP with the default l0 sensitivity.
 
## Additional Context
For now these methods are probably enough to use in PyDP:
https://github.com/google/differential-privacy/blob/b351a7f540c7cd8ff1c182ed3d780ebf403c68b0/cc/algorithms/algorithm.h#L212-L222
because I don't think there is any direct access to mechanisms in PyDP.

**Expected behavior**

I'm expecting oathkeeper hydrator  to connect to my custom backend and add the specific header to the request and forward it to the defined backend.

**Environment**

* Version:  "v0.0.48"
* Environment: Deployed with Helm in DigitalOcean managed Kubernetes cluster

**Additional context**

If I connect to my cluster and try to run the following curl command to my user-service:

```
curl --location --request POST 'http://localhost:8585/auth/hydrator' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--header 'Authorization: Bearer XXXXXXXXX.EuqjbTAMaUYVdw58PTAss2lOLLqyfaUkpoyWvY4uIVw' \
--data-raw '{
  "subject": "XXXXXXXXXX.DygsxJ_wkPA6PGGPdV4OpdBNOu53hma73oc_ivxLU2Q",
  "extra": {},

}'
```

I get the following response:

```json
{
    "subject": "XXXXXXXXX.DygsxJ_wkPA6PGGPdV4OpdBNOu53hma73oc_ivxLU2Q",
    "header": {
        "X-User-Id": "28426fa8-54ea-40f6-acbd-a317d18b8f03"
    }
}
```

I think the implementation in my user-service works as expected and returns the right format.

Does anyone has an idea where the problem might be ?

Title: [Bug]: Some Videos Default to Wrong Audio Track (v0.22.0 Beta)
Body:
### Guidelines

- [X] I have encountered this bug in the [latest release of FreeTube](https://github.com/FreeTubeApp/FreeTube/releases).
- [X] I have encountered this bug in the [official downloads of FreeTube](https://github.com/FreeTubeApp/FreeTube#official-downloads).
- [X] I have searched the issue tracker for [open](https://github.com/FreeTubeApp/FreeTube/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue) and [closed](https://github.com/FreeTubeApp/FreeTube/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed) issues that are similar to the bug report I want to file, without success.
- [X] I have searched the [documentation](https://docs.freetubeapp.io/) for information that matches the description of the bug I want to file, without success.
- [X] This issue contains only one bug.

### Describe the bug

Some videos consistently load in the first available audio track. This is almost always the wrong audio track for videos with multiple tracks, and it seems to ignore the track marked as "original". As an example, the following video, for which I've also included a screenshot of the audio tracks panel opened, defaults to German: 

https://youtu.be/gE6PjvcyUMU


I believe this is recent behavior, as it didn't seem to occur in the past even on videos with multiple audio tracks, but I can't speak with full certainty.

I've checked the documentation to little avail, as I presumed I somehow set a setting wrong. 

I've also checked the Issues page, and found this mentioned at least 3 times, but generally marked as solved in 2022 or 2023. Yet this is clearly occurring to me, and I've tested it on two separate devices, one of which I ensured was a fresh install with no pre-existing configs, imported playlists, etc. 

### Expected Behavior

Presumably, Freetube should default to the original audio track. Barring that, it should at least choose based on the Locale Preference.

usability issue

v0.22.0 Beta

Title: [Backend] Sovrn Email connectors for Consent requests
Body:
# Description

- Add a new `sovrn` email connector 
- test email and advanced settings identities are the inputs.  the recipient email and third party vendor name should be hardcoded to the connector
- Require at least one identity type to exist before saving connector
- Create a new privacy request status to reflect consent emails that are awaiting send.


# Batching
- Exit privacy request processing before completing if there are emails that need to be sent - put the privacy request in the new "awaiting_email_send" or similar status
- Weekly, query all privacy requests in this status. Pull the relevant details from each privacy request and send one email per email consent connector (currently just sovrn type).  
- Provided the email sends, add an audit log to the privacy request and re-queue to wrap up any remaining steps.



- Corresponding UI ticket for connector setup here: https://github.com/ethyca/fides/issues/2458

Title: Support github releases / packages / advisories
Body:
This might sound like an obvious question and maybe I'm wrong and this is supported or I didn't read the documentation correctly.

But I think it would be great if the Advisory Database integrated with Github Releases, Github Packages and Github Advisories for Github Projects.

# Use case

This could work well with dependabot and the new Dependency submission API. For example, I'm using Nix. Nix as a package manage does not typically use a centralized registry and rather uses "channels" that contain packages. 

However, nix packages many times fetch the sources from github. With the dependency submission API, a given nix dependency could be reported to be from github (or other supported ecosystem such as npm) and dependabot now would be able to report security vulnerability for nix dependencies.

Title: Add Certification Request Explanation Text to /demo Pages
Body:
## Background
The `/demo` page needs additional context to help users understand what certification requests are and how they can create them for testing purposes. Currently, there's no explanation of this core concept on the demo page or how users can get started with the application, which may cause confusion for users who are new to the system.


## User Story
As a developer or tester, I want to see a clear explanation of certification requests on the /demo page so that I understand what they are and how to create them manually for testing.


## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Add the following explanatory text to the `/demo/certifications/new` page: "A certification request is the case that a member responds to. In production, these are created in bulk through batch processes or API, but for testing you can create them manually. You can create it below."
- [ ] Add text on the `/demo `page (see below horizontal line)
- [ ] Text is positioned appropriately below the title
- [ ] Text styling is consistent with the rest of the page


_________________________________________________
**Below is the text to add to /demo page** 

### Exploring the application  
All routes below are relative to your current environment (e.g., localhost:3000 or medicaid.navateam.com). You can explore OSCER's different interfaces and workflows with the following instructions:

**Demo overview**. 
`/demo` Start here to see entrypoints to the different experiences in OSCER and understand the application's structure.

**Creating a Certification Request**. 
`/demo/certifications/new` A certification request is the case that a member responds to. In production, these are created in bulk through batch processes or API, but for testing you can create them manually.  

To experience the full workflow:

- Create a certification request using an email address you can access
- Configure different scenarios (lookback months, exemption triggers, etc.)
- Test automated exemptions by indicating pregnancy or other qualifying conditions
- Submit the request
_Note_: You can reuse the same email address for multiple certification requests—the system will automatically reset for that email.

**Member dashboard (or Client View)**. 
`/dashboard` This is the member-facing interface where clients respond to their certification requests. Follow the instructions on the dashboard to create an activity report or exemption request. Once submitted, you can navigate to the staff portal to view the submitted request. You must complete a certification request (see above) before you'll see any data in this view.
_Note_: Requires a certification request to be created first.

**Staff portal**. 
`/staff` This is the administrative interface where staff can review and process member certification responses.

**Additional resources**
- GitHub repo: https://github.com/navapbc/OSCER/blob/main/README.md
- API docs: https://medicaid.navateam.com/api/docs#post-/api/certifications

Title: Organization Tag Policy fails while executing via AWS Codepipeline, but works when applied via console
Treeshaking not working with maci library packages
Body:
We noticed that by importing just 1 function (genTallyResultCommitment) from the maci-core library, our web app size would double. Duplicating that function (as opposed to importing from maci-core) would bring the web app size back down.
 
 
 
 Here are the sizes of our web app:
 
 
 
 (import from maci-core)
 
 7,567.22 kB │ gzip: 3,538.62 kB
 
 
 
 (duplicate function locally) 
 
 3,669.37 kB │ gzip: 1,726.62 kB
 
 
 
 
 
 I tried different rollup treeshaking options on our vite.config file, without success.
 
 I tried adding "sideEffects: false" manually in the maci-core package in the local node_modules folder and still not working.
 
 
 
 While working on using the snarkjs API, I stumbled onto this issue (https://github.com/iden3/snarkjs/issues/152) which shows that ffjavascript library that maci-crypto depends on has side effects that might be causing treeshaking to not work. 
 
 
 
 For optimization, ffjavascript uses a global (globalThis variable) to pass back a handle for the consumer to terminate the threads.
 
 
 
 Note that maci-crypto only uses the utils functions in (ffjavascript)[https://github.com/privacy-scaling-explorations/maci/blob/dev/crypto/ts/index.ts#L9), may be duplicating those functions instead of `require('ffjavascript`) could reduce the bundle size of app?
 
 
 
 Also, moving the `genTallyResultCommitment` from maci-core to maci-crypto may help as we only need to import maci-crypto.
 
 
 
 We use all the hash and encrypt/decrypt functions in maci-crypto to generate key and encrypt/decrypt messages on our web app.
 
 
 
  Appreciate any suggestion on what to do to enable treeshaking and reduce our web app size.

Title: Security Issue: Implement Automated Dependency Management with Dependabot
Body:
## Problem Statement  
The SaralSeva project currently has **78+ security vulnerabilities** across all modules (`npm audit`).  
Without automated dependency management, the project is exposed to significant risks — critical for a government services platform handling citizen data.  

---

## Verified Vulnerabilities  
- **Backend**: `axios <1.12.0` (DoS), `undici`, `firebase`  
- **User Portal**: `pdfjs-dist` (Arbitrary JS exec), `dompurify <3.2.4` (XSS), `esbuild`  
- **Admin Portal**: `form-data` (CRITICAL), `rollup`, `cross-spawn`  
- **Employee Portal**: Same as Admin + PDF viewer issues  

---

## Proposed Solution  
Introduce **Dependabot** for automated dependency management:  
- Weekly npm updates (all modules)  
- Monthly GitHub Actions updates  
- Grouped updates (React ecosystem, UI libs, build tools)  
- Security updates always separate & prioritized  
- Major version bumps ignored for critical frameworks (React, Express, Mongoose)  

---

## Testing Evidence  
- ✅ Backend, User, Admin, Employee portals build successfully  
- ✅ No breaking changes (only config + docs added)  

---

## Files in PR  
- `.github/dependabot.yml` → Full config for all modules  
- `DEPENDABOT.md` → Workflow & customization guide  
- `SECURITY.md` → Vulnerability reporting policy  
- `README.md` → Dependabot section + badges  

---

## Expected Impact  
- Immediate: **78 vulnerabilities reduced → 0** (via auto PRs)  
- Long-term: Continuous weekly monitoring & patching  
- Reduced manual overhead, standardized workflow  

---

✅ **Ready for PR submission**  
Labels: `security`, `maintenance`, `critical`

Title: Privacy Portal (SideMenu): Can't change the colour of `a`
Tracker marks domain as failing if it encounters a READ_TIMEOUT
Body:
**Describe the bug**
When the Tracker encounters a READ_TIMEOUT error when scanning a domain it marks the domain as failing HTTPS, HSTS, Certificates, Protocols, Ciphers and Curves.  This lowers the compliance summaries for an organization.  READ_TIMEOUTs occur naturally on the internet.  They reflect a general communications error between the Tracker server, its hosting network and the target network/domain.  They do not indicate that the domain is not properly configured.  In most cases, it is normal to retry a connection after a READ_TIMEOUT, up to a maximum number of times.  It should not fail after the first READ_TIMEOUT.  If after retrying a few times it still gets a READ_TIMEOUT it makes more sense to me to mark the untestable properties as unknown/information instead of failed.

Doing a manual rescan will generally correct the domain issues, but it does not increase the compliance summaries.  Given the regular number of timeouts I am seeing in the tracker, I think this more likely points to a server/network issue with the tracker itself, but it appears on the site that our compliance is dropping.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Login to the Tracker
2. Go to the Domains section
3. Add a filter for HTTPS + EQUALS + FAIL
4. Notice the domains that are failing
5. Find a domain that was previously passing
6. Click on the View Results button for that domain
7. Notice the errors all stem from a READ_TIMEOUT error in the Tracker.
8. Notice the Protocols, Cipher Suites, Curves, Certificate Chain sections are all blank and marked as Failed.

**Expected behavior**
A READ_TIMEOUT error on the Tracker side should not mark the domain as failing.

**Screenshots**

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/43aed4d5-ff0d-47a0-9360-c76c2ff4339b)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc3b3b61-dced-43a9-b34f-1e59a885803c)

After a manual rescan

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae333772-24d9-4e32-bbb8-53570f9f04a7)

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Windows 11
 - Browser Mozilla Firefox
 - Version 134.0.2

**Additional context**
The Summaries tab of the Organization page does not update after a domain rescan.  So it regularly shows a lower compliance score caused by READ_TIMEOUTs on the Tracker side.

The user should have the ability to search the entire database, on any indexed field, such as demographic data, providers, Problem list, Medicine List, Allergy list, old problem list, old medicine list, PCP and associated MDs, insurance, race, language, ethnicity, date of visits, Vital signs, Flow sheet data, radiology data, legal documents (HCP, Advanced directives, HIPAA) smoking status, etc. For example, “Find all male patients, <65 yo, who have DM-2 and albuminuria and hypertension, and have not been seen in the last year, and whose most recent HBA1c>9, and is managed by Dr. XXX, is on lisinopril, and last SBP>160” or find all patients who are on 2 specified medications. Once a search is conducted, the resultant information should be able to be easily exported out of the EMR into an Excel or cvs document, for use as the physician feels is necessary.

Title: Arduino UNO R4 WiFi Support? `Error: no matching serial port found`
Using MQTT publish and subscribe in offline mode between devices connected to Greengrass core
Body:
I followed the Module 4 tutorial on [Interacting with devices in an AWS IoT Greengrass group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/greengrass/latest/developerguide/module4.html). I have a Raspberry Pi running the AWS IoT Greengrass Core. I have a group consisting of the core and the two devices (HelloWorld_Publisher, HelloWorld_Subscriber). The subscription rule is setup as mentioned in the tutorial. I have a laptop and the Raspberry Pi on the same local network. I fire up both the HelloWorld_Publisher and HelloWorld_Subscriber on my laptop using the [basicPubSub.py sample](https://github.com/aws/aws-iot-device-sdk-python/blob/master/samples/basicPubSub/basicPubSub.py). I am able to send and receive messages successfully.

Now, during the send, I cut off the Internet connection from my router to test offline connectivity. So the Internet is down but the local network is still working (I can ping from my laptop to the RPi). However, this makes the HelloWorld_Publisher crash with the following exception:

```
2020-09-02 23:15:33,683 - AWSIoTPythonSDK.core.protocol.mqtt_core - ERROR - Publish timed out
Traceback (most recent call last):
File "basicPubSub.py", line 120, in <module>
myAWSIoTMQTTClient.publish(topic, messageJson, 1)
File "/usr/local/lib/python2.7/site-packages/AWSIoTPythonSDK/MQTTLib.py", line 628, in publish
return self._mqtt_core.publish(topic, payload, QoS, False) # Disable retain for publish by now
File "/usr/local/lib/python2.7/site-packages/AWSIoTPythonSDK/core/protocol/mqtt_core.py", line 273, in publish
raise publishTimeoutException()
AWSIoTPythonSDK.exception.AWSIoTExceptions.publishTimeoutException
```

Why does this happen if the MQTT broker is running on the Greengrass Core on the RPi? Why is there a need for an Internet connection?

Is there some flag or something I can set to continue MQTT publish and subscribe in an offline mode?

Title: Migrating flows to other Node-RED instance invalidates FREE plan
Body:
### Bug Description

I was running Node-RED as an add-on in HA, but i am in the progress of migrating all flows to a separate Node-RED VM (on UNRAID). If i copy a flow containing VSH nodes from the add-on NR to the VM-NR, and after doing the account-linking via amazon etc. it considers the VSH nodes in the new VM as new ones and the free plan limit is enforced.

So it is no problem to use the same 7 FREE VSH nodes in the same Node-RED instance multipe times, but you can't use the same 7 FREE nodes in multiple Node-RED instances? Despite the account-linking?

How do i fix this? And is this also an issuw with the paid subscription?

### To Reproduce

- Use all 7 free nodes
- copy flow containg free nodes to 2nd instance of node-red

### Expected behavior

I expect all 7 free nodes to be available in every instance of Node-RED i'm using, or at least be able to transfer them to another instance.

### Virtual-Smart-Home Version

4.1.2

### Node-RED Version

3.1.5

### Node.js Version

16.20.0

### Plan

FREE

vsht-a123c2a9-fe91-4920-aa4b-2a82fee6a4f7

Title: Have anyone tried to deploy Seed Signer to a Raspberry Pi Pico?
Body:
The Raspberry Pi Pico has a considerable processing power, as compared to Arduino and other microcrontrolers.

Some advantages would be having no linux, small power draw to run from batteries, smaller downloads, but more importantly, the Pico is about $4 USD instead of the $5 if you manage to find the Zero 1.3, or $15 if you go for the Zero 2 W. The downside might be harder to source camera for the Pico.

Just to illustrate, in some parts of the world it is difficult to source the Zero. I can't find the 1.3 here in Brazil or sellers that would ship it from China. Sellers from china do have the Zero 2 but it costs ~ R$400 (around $79 USD), while I can find the Pico for ~ R$35 + ~R$10 shipping (about $10 USD total).

So I researched a bit, found the [WaveShare Pico LCD-1.3](https://www.waveshare.com/wiki/Pico-LCD-1.3), which is ~ R$40 and the [Arducam Pico supported cameras](https://www.arducam.com/raspberry-pi-pico-camera-modules/), which would be the most expensive hardware at $20 ~ $40 USD. 

If I understood correctly, in theory other SPI cameras could work, some start at ~$3 USD. But I haven't found any camera that has supported drivers for the Pico, so I won't risk it, unless someone more experienced offers some guidance.

I already oredered the pieces and I intend to hack around it. While I wait about 20 days for the 3 parts to arrive, I was wondering...

Anyone has any insight on the idea? Or if you know of anyone that already tried that? If those more engaged with the project considered it and had a good reason to drop the idea? If Micro-Python can run the bitcoin libraries or I would need to go down to C (which I am less familiar) And if there is any top of your head advice about it? Any comment whatsoever would be appreciated. Thanks!

Title: chore: upgrade lodash when available
Body:
there is a medium security vulnerability in a lodash function 

```text
Prototype Pollution
Vulnerable module: lodash
Introduced through: lodash@4.17.15 and csvtojson@2.0.10
Detailed paths
Introduced through: @mindconnect/mindconnect-nodejs@mindsphere/mindconnect-nodejs#c6084de5bad0303d94b9d2104ecc6e29d53e5798 › lodash@4.17.15
Remediation: Open PR to patch lodash@4.17.15.
Introduced through: @mindconnect/mindconnect-nodejs@mindsphere/mindconnect-nodejs#c6084de5bad0303d94b9d2104ecc6e29d53e5798 › csvtojson@2.0.10 › lodash@4.17.15
Remediation: Open PR to patch lodash@4.17.15.
Overview
lodash is a modern JavaScript utility library delivering modularity, performance, & extras.

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Prototype Pollution. The function zipObjectDeep can be tricked into adding or modifying properties of the Object prototype. These properties will be present on all objects.
```

This function is not used by the library. We ill upgrade lodash once the new lodash version is released.

Title: Generate SMPTE Timecode on the Pi
Body:
It would be cool if the Pi could also output standard [SMPTE Timecode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SMPTE_timecode) so it could be a reliable timecode source for media production, with equipment that accepts TC inputs.

From a cursory glance, I found a 7-year-old project called [piltc](https://github.com/edwar64896/piltc) by @edwar64896, which is aimed directly at the Pi, but has not been updated since the Pi 3B+ was the mainstream Pi, and I believe it used the 3.5mm audio jack, which the Pi 5 doesn't have (natively, at least).

There's also [vtc-py](https://github.com/opencinemac/vtc-py), a "SMTPE video timecode library for Python", and I found [pico-timecode](https://github.com/mungewell/pico-timecode) from @mungewell, which runs on a Pico using the PIO blocks.

I wonder if the same kind of setup could be run through the RP1's PIO (similar to how it's used to [bash out composite video](https://www.raspberrypi.com/news/how-we-added-interlaced-video-to-raspberry-pi-5/), I believe?

Finally, I found [pam](https://github.com/martim01/pam), a project by @martim01 that takes in AES67 or analog audio and pull LTC data out of it.

At this point, this is merely a curiosity for me—however, I'd like to slowly convert my studio over to recording devices that are synced, and timecode seems to be the primary method for that. Right now, after every video I record, I have to either sync with Final Cut Pro (not a horrible thing if I remembered to leave mics on all my cameras... but a disaster if I forget), or I have to adjust video/audio sync by nudging the audio track three frames back (when using my BlackMagicDesign recorder/monitor, which has a 3-frame delay from my camera's HDMI output, versus the no-delay analog mic signal coming off my 528E.

Hi AWS team, 

we are a bit stuck with a critical issue we are facing with the SDK since 2 days (details below).

**Describe the bug**
TLS channel shutdown by the task-scheduler immediately after host resolution resulting in infinite RECONNECTING <>  AWS_ERROR_MQTT_UNEXPECTED_HANGUP loop (Eating a lot of data !!).
SDK connection to the endpoint is never established. TLS opening and closing of sessions at a very fast pace causing tremendous data usage burst (we got several hundred $ of data roaming bill on a field device due to the sudden issue).

**SDK version number**
Tested with 1.5.12 & 1.5.14 and matching aws-crt in each case

**Platform/OS/Device**
Armhf device (Cortex-A7)
Docker container based on ubuntu 20.04

**To Reproduce (observed behavior)**

Standard use of the SDK was observed and the device was running for 10 days before the reconnection loop occurred. After that, the device was never able to reconnect properly to our endpoint and the reconnection loop would always be present. Behavior changed on 30.04.2021 after 10 days of normal operation (connections & publish every 3 minutes). The certificates & CA are not expired and renewed device registration under a new certificate did not help. Update from SDK 1.5.12 to 1.15.14 did not help either.

```
AWS_KEEP_ALIVE_SECS = 30

    # setup AWS connection
    io.init_logging(io.LogLevel.Debug, 'stderr')
    event_loop_group = io.EventLoopGroup(1)
    host_resolver = io.DefaultHostResolver(event_loop_group)
    client_bootstrap = io.ClientBootstrap(event_loop_group, host_resolver)

    client_id = "auto-%s" % str(uuid.uuid4()).upper()
    aws_mqtt = mqtt_connection_builder.mtls_from_path(
        endpoint=args.endpoint,
        cert_filepath="%s/device.crt" % (args.provision_location),
        pri_key_filepath="%s/device.key" % (args.provision_location),
        client_bootstrap=client_bootstrap,
        ca_filepath="%s/AmazonRootCA1.pem" % (args.cert_location),
        on_connection_interrupted=aws_on_connection_interrupted,
        on_connection_resumed=aws_on_connection_resumed,z
        client_id=client_id,
        clean_session=False,
        keep_alive_secs=AWS_KEEP_ALIVE_SECS)
```

**Expected behavior**

No unexpected hangup. And no infinite reconnection loop.

Title: apt-key is being deprecated, use replacement for tor pgp key
Body:
https://stadicus.github.io/RaspiBolt/raspibolt_22_privacy.html#installing-tor

Key management with apt-key is getting phased out. Replacement is by downloading key into a keyring file, taken from https://www.linuxuprising.com/2021/01/apt-key-is-deprecated-how-to-add.html:

```
wget -O- https://deb.torproject.org/torproject.org/A3C4F0F979CAA22CDBA8F512EE8CBC9E886DDD89.asc | gpg --dearmor | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/torproject-keyring.gpg
```
and adding a signed-by field to a separate sources file (`/etc/apt/sources.list.d/torproject.list`):
```
deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/torproject-keyring.gpg] https://deb.torproject.org/torproject.org buster main
deb-src [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/torproject-keyring.gpg] https://deb.torproject.org/torproject.org buster main
```

I tested this on Ubuntu 20.10. I don't know this is relevant for Raspberry OS.

Title: "Server Certificate Verification failed" with Custom Domain
Body:
### Describe the bug

Hi,

I wanted to report this issue we have been experiencing while trying to switch the IoT Core to custom domain. 

Understood that V2 is the solution and should have resolved most issues, we do plan to gradually migrate to V2. 

However the thing is we still do have a large number of legacy hardware (Ubuntu 18.04) deployed in the field that we need to support, which makes it a major risk & high cost for us to bring those to V2. 

Therefore, we would really appreciate if anyone could provide some insights on the issues with the IoT Core custom domain work with V1, so we can save our legacy hardware.

# Issue
We are experiencing `Server Certificate Verification failed.` during the SSL handshake when connecting to our custom domain, which is also reproducible with the PubSub example. 

However, the SDK works perfectly when simply connects to the ATS endpoint. 

The only thing we swapped is the endpoint URL in the config file of the SDK, from ATS endpoint to our custom domain. Everything else is properly configured including the ACM SSL certs, VPC endpoint to the iot:data plane, etc.

# What we have tried
1. Tried both IoT CPP SDK V2 and IoT Python SDK to connect to the same custom domain: PubSub example works without problem for both SDKs, and MQTT test client can pub&sub normally
2. Connect to ATS endpoint using CPP SDK V1: works
3. Reinstall both OpenSSL 1.1.1 and 1.1.0g and recompile CPP SDK V1: issue persists
4. Test with `openssl s_client -connect <ipv4_addr>:443  -CAfile certs/rootCA.crt` as well as `openssl s_client -connect <custom_domain>:443  -CAfile certs/rootCA.crt`: Both showed verification `OK`.

However we did notice without specifying the SNI, the s_client always uses the amazonaws SSL cert over our custom domain cert. The results are the following:

Title: Reconsider the WiFi event API
Body:
## Problem Statement

We expose users to the events emitted by the WiFi drivers via the wait_for_event family of functions and also via the events module.

By doing that we

- assume users are familiar with the events (especially when to expect which events)
- assume none of the events will get removed from the drivers (marking our Event-enum as non-exhaustive allows us to add new events but not to remove events - if something like that happens in future we might or might not be able to "emulate" removed events)
- the wait_for_event functions don't have a way to tell the payload of events (while the unstable "event" module does)
- "force" users to know enough about the events since some very simple use-cases require to use the wait_for_event async functions (e.g. to know about a disconnect event)

So at least for simpler things we should offer more specialized functionality like "waiting for station disconnected" - and ideally return an error if we are in the wrong state and we should also return the details (e.g. the disconnect reason in this case).

For the basic use-cases the amount of additional / specialized functions wouldn't be too much but it would allow us to hide details (which users usually don't care about) from the user.

While offering a way to listen for events is something that advanced use-cases might benefit from, having that as a stable API and even forcing users to use it for very basic use-cases is problematic for the reasons listed above.

## Proposal

Instead of offering (and even more forcing users to use) a stable event listening API we should offer functionality to support actual use-cases.

(Non-exhaustive?) list of basic use-cases to cover initially

- STA: connect (user-initiated, should return the payload) and disconnect (user-initiated OR externally initiated) - we need to return additional information from connect/disconnect and a way to get notified of a non-user-initiated disconnect (including additional information, e.g. the disconnect reason)
- AP: a way to know about connected and disconnected STAs - these are not user initiated, there is important additional information the user needs / wants to know about

(I intentionally don't propose a way how we want to implement it here - we first need consent if we want to go into this direction or not.)

Basically this boils down to the question: Do we want to provide a high level, use-case focused API or do we want to "just expose what the drivers allow"


## Future use-cases we might want to support later (non-exhaustive)

- WPS: We currently don't support WPS at all but to support it (besides of other things) we need to process WIFI_EVENT_STA_WPS_ER_SUCCESS, WIFI_EVENT_STA_WPS_ER_FAILED, WIFI_EVENT_STA_WPS_ER_TIMEOUT, WIFI_EVENT_STA_WPS_ER_PIN - some of these events carry important information which needs to be used. This seems to be a good fit for a more use-case centric API

- FTM: We currently don't support FTM at all but to support it (besides of other things) we need to process WIFI_EVENT_FTM_REPORT which carries the important information - it's not just waiting for single events and get the payload but needs continuously getting events and process them which doesn't fit the `wait_for_X` API

- SmartConfig / ESP-Touch: We don't support this yet and we can't even process any of the SC_EVENT_* events. It seems to be a good fit for a use-case centric API.

---

Supersedes #4364

Title: Setup frontend unit tests
Improvements to historical mempool chart x-axis labels
Body: ## Background Recently we migrated the project to the Apache echarts graph library, the primary reason being so that we could implement a mouseover legend, which appears when you hover over the historical mempool data, as well as it being needed for new charts and graphs we want to implement in the upcoming mining dashboard. The migration to echarts is nearly complete, but one major task remaining is polishing the x-axis labels, as originally reported in #842 by Murch who noticed they were incorrectly positioned, i.e. if you hover over "May 30" it would not be exactly at midnight on May 30. Therefore the remaining work is to fix the x-axis labels so they are both localized and accurate. Previously a WIP of this was attempted in PR #946 but it was not completed. Therefore this issue is to complete the WIP PR, which requires implementing changes in the forked echarts npm modules (https://github.com/mempool/echarts/pull/1 and https://github.com/mempool/ngx-echarts/pull/1) and other changes in mempool as necessary. ### Part 1: Localizing the label date/time strings This first part is pretty straightforward, as it just uses the Angular code to localize the timestamps. Of course, different date formats are appropriate for different timestamps, such as the following: 2 hour 24 hour 1 week 1 month 3 month 6 month 1 year ### Part 2: Fix inconsistent tick and label positions After localizing the timestamps, the following work must be done: 1) The x-axis labels becomes too large to fit and therefore need to be correctly spaced on the size of the user's browser display width: 2) On chart timespans greater than 1 week, the position of the "ticks" is not exactly on midnight of the date labels, and other places that are expected. This is the main complaint of the issue. To correct this, custom tick position is probably required, which might require modifying the mempool backend to return such customized time points, or further changes inside our fork of the echarts library, or both. 3) Testing. After implementing all of the above, the new version should be consistent with current production mempool.space data and match completely - lots of testing of all functionality, including "zoom in" on the chart etc. in various timeframes will be necessary.

Title: Hardfault in library (Guessing Memory address fault)
Add GDB code before loading with OpenOCD
Body:
I was using VS Code in WSL + OpenOCD (running on Windows native) + Cortex Debug (remote connection) successfully and happily.
But now the microcontroller we are developing has a locked flash and bootloader as feature, so when launching a debug session the file download will always fail.

I already have a GDB script that unlocks the flash. Is there some way I can let Cortex Debug run this script before the file download starts?

I looked at https://github.com/Marus/cortex-debug/blob/master/debug_attributes.md , but the option seems to relate to command to e.g. OpenOCD itself.

Title: Long disconnects when using MQTT over websockets
Body:
Confirm by changing [ ] to [x] below to ensure that it's a bug:
- [x] I've searched for [previous similar issues](https://github.com/aws/aws-iot-device-sdk-java-v2/issues) and didn't find any solution

**Known Issue**
- [x] I'm using ATS data type endpoint: the endpoint should look like `<prefix>-ats.iot.<region>.amazonaws.com`

**Describe the bug**
Our IoT clients use MQTT over websockets and connect via proxy. The clients regularly disconnect and immediately (within a second) connect again, which is as expected. However, sometimes the period of time between a disconnect and a connect is much longer. In the log below you can see that at 2021-04-09 10:15:01.847 the client disconnected and only connected again after 12 seconds. How can that be?

Also below is the CRT log from the SDK. Note that the times in CloudWatch log are in UTC+0 while the ones in the CRT log are in EDT.

**SDK version number**
1.2.12

**Platform/OS/Hardware/Device**
Amazon Linux 2

**Expected behavior**
